character_sheet: A stocky human thief: a belly block, a chest block, a head that turns with the look, two arms splayed 28 degrees and two legs (ModelBandP.java:31-79; 7 parts on a 64x128 sheet). The same rig wears one of two skins, bandit or pirate, rolled once on its first tick and synched (BandP.java:121-128, BandPRenderer.java:39). It is hostile but tough rather than deadly: 100 HP, 1 damage, 18 armour, speed 0.32 (MobStats.BANDP, :89-98), 1000 XP. Every twelfth tick it picks a non-creative player, a villager, a girlfriend or a boyfriend in sight within 20 blocks (:243-265), walks at it at 1.25 (:164) and, within 3 blocks, hits it (:159-160, doHurtTarget); a hit that lands on a player steals one item - armour first, helmet to boots, else the last filled inventory slot - into a 100-slot stash that spills on death (:178-212, :219-241). It opens doors (:83), heads indoors (:86), walks through villages (:78) and strolls (:80); it spawns by day above y 100 within 36 blocks of a villager, never near another (:300-311). Read it as a swaggering brigand: a heavy stride with the arms swinging opposite the legs and the torso twisting, a fidget at rest, a snatch when it hits.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.0 of the rig (BandPRenderer.java:29; no scale override) on a 64x128 sheet (ModelBandP.java:79); the hitbox is 0.75 x 1.75 (ModEntities.java:45-47); shadow 1.0 (BandPRenderer.java:31). Two textures on one rig: bandp_bandit.png (getWhat() == 0) and bandp_pirate.png.

labels.belly: belly (the lower torso; bounces and twists with the stride)
labels.head: head (turns and pitches with the look)

groups.name: gait
groups.axis: x (legs and arms) / y (the belly's twist)
groups.amplitude: legs: pi x 0.25 = 0.785 rad (45 deg) x the walking speed above the 0.1 threshold; arms: the same angle in opposition to the legs; belly: half of it as a twist about y (22 deg); standing (at or below the threshold): the legs and the belly twist hold 0 and the arms take the arm_sway rhythm instead
groups.plain: a marching stride: the legs swing in opposition, the arms swing against the legs, and the belly twists with the step
groups.math: walking: a = cos(t * 1.3 * 0.4) * pi * 0.25 * limbSwingAmount; lleg.xRot = a; rleg.xRot = -a; larm.xRot = -a; rarm.xRot = a; belly.yRot = -a / 2; standing: a = 0
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.3 x 0.4 (wingspeed, ModelBandP.java:21): the natural period is 2 pi / 0.52 = 12.1 ticks

groups.name: belly_bounce
groups.amplitude: 0.07 rad rest (4 deg forward), then walking: pi x 0.025 = 0.079 rad (4.5 deg) x the walking speed at 2.6 x 0.4 - twice the gait rate; standing: pi x 0.005 = 0.016 rad (0.9 deg) at 0.6 x 0.4 (omega 0.24, period 26.2 ticks)
groups.plain: the belly bounces twice per stride on the move and breathes barely at rest
groups.math: belly.xRot = 0.07 + (walking ? cos(t * 2.6 * 0.4) * pi * 0.025 * limbSwingAmount : cos(t * 0.6 * 0.4) * pi * 0.005)
groups.phase: the walking-speed threshold selects the rhythm (ModelBandP.java:87, 91)
groups.omega_note: the walking phase is ageInTicks x 2.6 x 0.4: the natural period is 2 pi / 1.04 = 6 ticks (twice the gait rate); standing 2 pi / 0.24 = 26.2 ticks

groups.name: arm_sway
groups.amplitude: standing only: pi x 0.02 = 0.063 rad (3.6 deg) at 0.3 x 0.4, the arms in opposition; walking, the arms follow the gait group instead
groups.plain: at rest the arms sway slowly against each other
groups.math: standing: s = cos(t * 0.3 * 0.4) * pi * 0.02; larm.xRot = -s; rarm.xRot = s
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.3 x 0.4: the natural period is 2 pi / 0.12 = 52.4 ticks

behaviour: Two branches on the walking speed (ModelBandP.java:87-95). Walking (above 0.1): the cosine of the age x 1.3 x 0.4 (wingspeed, :21), x pi x 0.25, x the walking speed swings the left leg forward and the right back (45 degrees at full speed every 12.1 ticks); the arms take the same angle the other way (left arm back with the left leg forward, :99-100); the belly twists about the vertical by half of it (:101) and bounces about x at twice the rate - 0.07 rad plus the cosine of the age x 2.6 x 0.4 x pi x 0.025 x the walking speed (:98).

Standing (at or below 0.1): the legs and the belly twist hold 0; the belly breathes 0.9 degrees at 0.6 x 0.4 (:93, :98) and the arms sway 3.6 degrees against each other at 0.3 x 0.4 (:94, :99-100) - a fidget every 52 ticks.
The head follows the look in yaw and pitch (:102-103), so the LookAtPlayerGoal and RandomLookAroundGoal (BandP.java:81-82) are visible; the chest never moves.

There is no attacking flag: the synched DATA_WHAT (BandP.java:42-43) is the skin roll, not a state; the hit (doHurtTarget :160, within 3 blocks every twelfth tick) and the theft (:161, :178-212) have no pose of their own.
Nothing floats it: no FloatGoal is registered (:70-87) and its stroll avoids water (:80).

in `attack`: a punch with the shoulder behind it - the hit (BandP.java:160) has no pose today

formulas: `ModelBandP.setupAnim` (ModelBandP.java:83-104; orig ModelBandP.java:79-94 in `render` (func_78088_a, :71-102; func_78087_a at :110-112 is a bare super call), wingspeed 0.4 from `new ModelBandP(0.4f)` in orig ClientProxyOreSpawn.java:504): while the walking speed is above a tenth the leg swing is the cosine of the age in ticks times 1.3 times 0.4, times pi, times 0.25, times the walking speed, the belly bounce the cosine of the age times 2.6 times 0.4, times pi, times 0.025, times the walking speed, and the arm swing equals the leg swing; at or below it the leg swing is 0, the belly breathes by the cosine of the age times 0.6 times 0.4, times pi, times 0.005 and the arms sway by the cosine of the age times 0.3 times 0.4, times pi, times 0.02; the left leg pitches by the leg swing and the right by its negative, the belly pitches by 0.07 plus the bounce and yaws by minus half the leg swing, the left arm pitches by the negative of the arm swing and the right by it, and the head yaws by the look yaw in radians and pitches by the look pitch in radians. The walk position and the entity's state play no part. The GeckoLib hook is the same (BandPGeoReplacement.applyCustomAnimations).
